item.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
item.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

item.title: America’s Naval Disaster
item.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

item.title: Humanoid Robots and China’s Vision of the Future
item.description: China’s humanoid robots are more than a showcase of state ambition. They reveal how differently we interpret visions of the technological future depending on who builds them.

item.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
item.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

item.title: How the Chinese Government Has Controlled the Narrative on the Tibet Floods
item.description: Chinese state media’s handling of the Tibet floods is following its usual pattern of restricted coverage, censorship, and emphasizing positive news.

item.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
item.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

item.title: Human Rights Are Essential to Australia’s Interests
item.description: Governments such as Australia’s need to recognize that defending civil society and a free press throughout the region and beyond are not luxuries but central to a democratic resurgence.

item.title: US Unpredictability Is Giving Its Asian Allies New Reasons to Cooperate
item.description: Across the Indo-Pacific, several of the United States’ closest partners are investing more heavily in relationships with one another – and, increasingly, with Europe.

item.description: Critics have decried the opaque agreement as oligarchic and colonialist.

item.title: In Cambodia, Floating Houses Are Stuck Aground as Climate Change Takes Hold
item.description: Researchers are seeing a change in Cambodian weather patterns as climate change takes hold across the region.

item.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
item.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

item.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
item.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.

item.title: Australia Should Work With China, Not Try to Contain It
item.description: China’s growing power is reshaping the region. Australia should respond with diplomacy and stronger economic ties rather than a military confrontation it cannot hope to win.
